framing_note: A document-native read of TMICC's Annual Report — a report map and a chronological list of dated strategic checkpoints the report itself states, each with a page citation. Distinct from the Strategy tab (which back-traces commitments to initiatives) and the Timeline tab (which correlates TMICC against competitors/macro events) — this panel stays inside what one single document says, in the order/structure it says it.

source_document.title: The Magnum Ice Cream Company N.V. — Annual Report 2025
source_document.filing_type: Form 20-F (Annual Report), filed with the U.S. SEC — the SEC's annual-report equivalent for a foreign private issuer. TMICC is Netherlands-incorporated and listed on NYSE, LSE, and Euronext Amsterdam, so it files a 20-F rather than a US-domestic 10-K; functionally the same disclosure role, which is why this panel is framed as a 10-K-style analyzer.
source_document.checked_for_newer_reports: Checked TMICC's investor relations site (corporate.magnumicecream.com/en/investors) and SEC EDGAR, 22 Sep 2026 — this FY2025 report remains the current, latest Annual Report; the FY2026 Annual Report isn't expected until early 2027. Two 2026 Form 6-K filings exist (interim/current disclosures, e.g. AGM results) but are not yet incorporated into this panel — gap, revisit next refresh.

strategic_checkpoints.detail: Three levers named explicitly: supply chain transformation, overhead reduction, and technology-enabled operations. Designed to deliver savings over the medium term.
strategic_checkpoints.cross_reference: Strategy tab — headline commitment 'Cost / separation savings'

strategic_checkpoints.checkpoint: Demerger from Unilever completed; TMICC began trading as an independent listed company
strategic_checkpoints.detail: Described in both the Board Chair and CEO updates as the defining milestone of the year.

strategic_checkpoints.checkpoint: €3 billion debut bond issuance across four tranches (2029, 2031, 2034, 2037)
strategic_checkpoints.detail: Euro Medium Term Note programme, interest rate range 2.75%-4%, order book oversubscribed more than 7x. Financial liabilities rose to €3,416m (2024: €333m); average debt maturity 7.5 years. This is TMICC's real debt-maturity wall — worth tracking against future refinancing risk.

strategic_checkpoints.checkpoint: €300 million credit facility earmarked for the Indian ice cream business acquisition
strategic_checkpoints.detail: Financing detail behind the Kwality Wall's transaction (completed 30 Mar 2026, already tracked in the Ecosystem tab) — this is the specific facility funding it, not previously captured.

strategic_checkpoints.checkpoint: Full compliance with the 2025 Dutch Corporate Governance Code, Best Practice Provision 1.4.3(ii)-(iv)
strategic_checkpoints.detail: TMICC's own Board states it is not yet fully compliant as a newly-standalone company, and expects to close the gap by 2026. A real, self-disclosed governance checkpoint distinct from the Foundation Plan for Growth shareholder-dissent issue tracked elsewhere.

strategic_checkpoints.checkpoint: Exit all remaining Transitional Services Agreements (TSAs) with Unilever
strategic_checkpoints.detail: TMICC still relies on Unilever for some transitional operational support post-demerger; full independence from these arrangements is targeted for end-2027.

strategic_checkpoints.checkpoint: Vanilla for Change programme — 80% of enrolled Madagascar farmers transitioned to regenerative agriculture; 1 million trees planted (up from 585,000 today), survival rate target rising from 40% to 65%
strategic_checkpoints.detail: Run with Symrise and Save the Children in the vanilla-producing Sava region of Madagascar.

strategic_checkpoints.checkpoint: New cabinet energy-efficiency technology begins rolling out on new freezer-cabinet purchases
strategic_checkpoints.detail: Connects directly to the freezer-cabinet fleet risk already flagged in the Ecosystem tab (TMICC's largest single emissions source, and a fleet it doesn't own).

strategic_checkpoints.checkpoint: Net Zero ambition across Scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions
strategic_checkpoints.detail: Explicit scenario-planning horizons defined elsewhere in the report: near-term 2026-2030, medium-term 2031-2039 for climate transition-risk modelling.

clarifications.topic: "Potential acquisition in India" in the report's cautionary statement (p.235)
clarifications.clarification: This appears only inside the standard forward-looking-statements disclaimer boilerplate (a list of example statement categories), not as a fresh, separate disclosure. Read in context, it most plausibly refers to the already-known Kwality Wall's transaction rather than signalling a second, undisclosed India deal — flagged here so it isn't mistaken for new news.
